title: Gnocchi al Pomodoro
subtitle: Pillowy potato dumplings in tomato sauce
excerpt: Homemade potato gnocchi are lighter and more delicate than anything from a packet, and the technique is straightforward once you understand the dough. A simple, quick tomato sauce with basil and parmesan is all they need.
sourceNotes: Potato gnocchi became widespread across northern and central Italy from the eighteenth century onwards, after potatoes arrived from the Americas. Each region has its own variation; this version follows the classic northern Italian approach of potato, flour, and egg yolk.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked gnocchi on a lined tray, then transfer to a bag. Cook from frozen in boiling water, adding 1 to 2 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make and shape the gnocchi up to 4 hours ahead and keep refrigerated on a floured tray.

content.text: The key to light gnocchi is using floury potatoes such as Maris Piper or King Edward, and working the dough as little as possible. The more you knead, the more gluten develops and the heavier the gnocchi become. Use just enough flour to bring the dough together.

items.prepNote: floury variety such as Maris Piper, unpeeled

content.text: Boil the potatoes whole and unpeeled in well-salted water for 25 to 30 minutes until completely tender. Drain and leave until cool enough to handle, then peel.
Pass the potatoes through a ricer or fine sieve onto a clean work surface. Spread out and leave to cool for 5 minutes so the steam escapes.
Make a well in the potato, add the egg and flour, and bring together with your hands until just combined into a soft dough. Do not overwork it.
Divide the dough into 6 pieces. Roll each piece into a rope about 2cm thick on a lightly floured surface. Cut into 2cm pieces.

For the sauce, warm the olive oil in a wide pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook gently for 2 minutes until lightly golden. Add the tinned tomatoes and a pinch of salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, then add the basil leaves.

Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the gnocchi in batches; they are ready 30 seconds after they float to the surface. Lift out with a slotted spoon directly into the tomato sauce.
Toss the gnocchi gently in the sauce to coat. Serve immediately with parmesan grated on top.

items.symptom: Gnocchi are falling apart in the water.
items.cause: The dough was too wet, usually from watery potatoes.
items.fix: Add flour a tablespoon at a time until dough just holds.

items.cause: Too much flour was worked in, or the dough was over-kneaded.
items.fix: Use the minimum flour needed and stop mixing when combined.

items.cause: They were not dusted with enough flour before cooking.
items.fix: Lay on a well-floured tray in a single layer before cooking.
